answer: Each claim must set a marble on a glacier face shaped by the last close hash, carved only from its own verified jobs, its grain that history frozen in ice. Three peers shine a lantern through it: the grain must match the glacier's ice-core record. A marble carved from borrowed jobs shows the wrong grain and the claim drops with its 115 POA fee burned. Marbles from one operator share one face, and each new marble adds its weight, so ten marbles weigh 55 units and one bad grain calves the whole face, sinking all ten claims. One face holds one identity; a marble cannot be re-cut across clones.
